Note NLP Accessor API Reference¶

Back to Note API Reference

Note::nlp() is the linguistic operation boundary for Note. It keeps generic text mechanics on Note while collecting operations whose meaning depends on tokens, sentences, language, document markup, corpus cleanup, phonetics, or linguistic set comparison.

The accessor is zero-overhead plumbing: obtaining it performs no transform and does not enlarge Note. Every terminal method is still batched over all cells and returns either a shape-preserving Note or a closed TokenBatch containing Text tokens and Int64 offsets.

TokenBatch has its own method reference. Use it to learn the flattened token Note, cumulative offsets, defined/empty state, and borrowed-reference lifetime shared by every ragged NLP result.

Shape-preserving Text Note

Canonical Surface¶

The accessor deliberately omits duplicate spellings. tokens() is the word tokenizer; there is no parallel words() alias. sentences() is the sentence tokenizer. char_ngrams(n) and word_ngrams(n) cover every width, so fixed bigrams() and trigrams() aliases are not part of the public surface.

Every public accessor method has one canonical handwritten page below. The list is ordered A-Z, and each page participates in the same family-aware previous/next chain.

Result Types And Row Boundaries¶

Shape-preserving analyses and cleanup methods return Note. Variable-length extractors and token transforms return TokenBatch; use batch.tokens() for the flat Text payload and batch.offsets() for cumulative cell boundaries. Neither accessor belongs to root Note, which is why offsets appears only in the standalone TokenBatch sidebar.
